clues: This port in the Philippines once served as the main sea gate of Manila. Big trade ships from far lands came and went from its shore.
This shore place has two clear times of year for rain. A long wet spell runs from May to November, then a dry spell from December to April.
This port was the seat of its province from the year that province was set up, 1614. It kept that seat till the role moved on in 1954.
Big ships once left this port for Acapulco in Mexico. They were the great galleons of a famed trade that crossed the wide Pacific.
One famed isle that forms part of this place is Corregidor. It is an isle with a big past, and its name is known far and wide.
